sections.title: Start script for Unix systems
sections.what: A short launcher for Mac and Linux. It moves into the folder the script lives in, then runs scripts/task.py with the start argument using python3.
sections.why: Likely reason: moving to the script's own folder first means it works no matter where the user runs it from.
sections.watch_out: python3 must be on the PATH and scripts/task.py must exist, neither of which is visible in this file.

summary: A small shell script for Mac and Linux. It moves into the project folder and starts the app through scripts/task.py start.
purpose: Gives Mac and Linux users a one-step way to start the app.
why: Likely reason: changing into the script's own folder lets it work from any location. The code shows this.
how: The script finds its own folder, changes into it, and runs the Python task file with the start command. It stops on any error.
inputs: python3 on the system path, and the project files.
outputs: A running server and a browser window.
risks: It uses the system python3 rather than the project environment, but the task file then sets up what it needs.
debug: If python3 is not found, install Python. If the app does not start, run the bootstrap task first.
